newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Divided Mostar to see new local election?.
newsitem.headline: Divided Mostar to see new local election?.

text.p: The ethnically partitioned Bosnian city of Mostar might hold new municipal elections this summer as part of countrywide polling for local authorities, a Western official said on Saturday.
The first post-war polls there last year failed to unite the Moslem and Croat communities.
"Yes, there may be local election in Mostar, but it's still being discussed," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

Bosnian's state-run news agency ONASA said on Friday local Moslem and Croat officials held separate meetings with the director of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Mostar on the isssue in the southern city.

The OSCE supervised Bosnia's first elections last September after a peace treaty halted the war in December 1995. The vote re-elected the same nationalist parties that were in power when fighting erupted in the former Yugoslav republic.
Mostar held its separate elections for city council three months earlier under European Union supervision in an effort to unify the city.
After complaints of irregularities, a single city administration and a mayor were installed in August but that did not bring unity or reduce tensions and violence.
The Western official told Reuters the whole issue was only beginning to come into focus, adding that nothing could be confirmed or denied at this stage.
Last year's voting in Mostar gave a chance to hundreds of people, mostly Moslems expelled by separatist Croat militia, to cross former frontlines in the city and vote in their pre-war municipalities.
